ideas.painful_workflow: Entrants have to prove a working project, runnable repo, README setup path, demo coverage, /feedback Codex Session ID, and deadline-safe completeness across separate artifacts before changes lock after July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT.
ideas.current_workaround: Manual checklists, README rewrites, commit browsing, and late Devpost form review, usually without a reproducible link between claims and artifacts.
ideas.imported_mechanism: mechanism-000: execution-to-claim provenance binding from trace-grounded execution auditing.
ideas.core_computation: Ingest git commits, README sections, test logs, demo script bullets, Codex session metadata, and declared GPT-5.6/Codex contribution claims; normalize them into a graph that binds each claim to a commit hash, command output, session identifier, or missing evidence marker; then run timestamp, artifact-presence, and reproducibility checks against the required submission package.
ideas.last_mile_action: Generates a locked submission bundle: patched README checklist, evidence manifest, demo script diff, failing readiness gates, and a shareable judge-test link that can be re-run locally or in a sandbox.
ideas.visible_transformation: The demo starts with a repo showing unsupported claims and missing submission artifacts, then after running the recorder shows specific claims turning from red to green only when linked to commit/test/session evidence, while the generated manifest and README are written to disk.
ideas.sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
ideas.technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
ideas.why_now: The submission window closes on July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT, changes are barred after that point, and Stage One can reject projects that fail basic viability or required-tool fit.
ideas.killer_demo: Use a sample Build Week repo with a vague README claim like 'built with Codex and GPT-5.6' and no setup proof. Run the tool, watch it fail the package, add a Codex Session ID and test command output, then re-run to produce a verified evidence manifest and a judge-ready README section in under three minutes.
ideas.hard_to_fake_advantage: It does not grade the idea or summarize the repo. It checks immutable identifiers, timestamps, command outputs, and evidence reachability, making unsupported contribution claims visible before submission lock.
ideas.gpt_5_6_role: GPT-5.6 performs the central constrained reasoning transformation and emits evidence-linked structured decisions
ideas.codex_build_role: Codex builds the executable prototype, test fixtures, evaluation harness, and records the required session
ideas.data_access_plan: Fetch the cited public source, cache a fixed fixture, and verify every demo input against it
ideas.testable_claim: Compared with a manual 20-item submission checklist baseline, the tool reduces unresolved required-artifact issues in a seeded repo from at least 6 to 0 and produces a reproducible evidence manifest in under 5 minutes on the demo machine.
ideas.demo_proof: Use a sample Build Week repo with a vague README claim like 'built with Codex and GPT-5.6' and no setup proof. Run the tool, watch it fail the package, add a Codex Session ID and test command output, then re-run to produce a verified evidence manifest and a judge-ready README section in under three minutes.

ideas.painful_workflow: Instead of proving broad prior-work boundaries, the user has a concrete defect: a submission claim, setup step, or required-tool explanation is wrong or unsupported, and fixing it means manually comparing the README, demo script, repo state, and official Build Week rules before editing the workflow text.
ideas.current_workaround: A teammate leaves comments in docs or chat, then someone manually rewrites the README and hopes the correction is specific enough and aligned with the official requirements.
ideas.imported_mechanism: mechanism-000: trace-grounded execution auditing from software verification and scientific reproducibility, adapted into a correction synthesizer. GPT-5.6 performs the material reasoning role: it compares each submission statement against verified evidence, repo traces, and command output, then proposes the smallest correction that removes unsupported language. Codex performs the material build role: it implements the repo scanner, README patcher, correction diff view, command runner, and /feedback-traceable workflow that writes the accepted correction back into the repository.
ideas.mechanism_origin: causal inference and software process mining
ideas.core_computation: The system ingests the README, package scripts, demo checklist, git metadata, and verified Build Week rule sources. It builds a claim-to-evidence graph, marks contradicted or unsupported statements, asks GPT-5.6 to generate a bounded replacement sentence with cited evidence IDs, then uses Codex-built patch machinery to apply only reviewer-approved corrections. Day 1: cache https://openai.devpost.com/rules and https://openai.devpost.com/details/faqs fixtures and define correction severity labels. Day 2: build README/demo-script claim extractor and evidence graph. Day 3: implement GPT-5.6 correction generation and contradiction checks. Day 4: add Codex-authored patch application, review UI, and rollback log. Day 5: record a before/after demo on a seeded repo with two false claims and one missing required explanation.
ideas.last_mile_action: Writes a verified correction directly into the workflow artifact: it opens a pull request or local patch that updates README/setup/demo text, inserts the matching evidence IDs, and adds a correction log entry showing data_access_status=verified for src-a90051657ad2 and src-9e3a619909fa.
ideas.visible_transformation: Before: the seeded README has 3 submission claims, with 2 unsupported or contradicted by verified rules evidence and 0 committed corrections. After: the correction run leaves 0 contradicted claims, commits 2 evidence-linked text repairs, and shows a reviewer-approved diff with the exact rule URL beside each change.

ideas.primary_user: Bootcamp instructors running live coding labs who need every learner to leave a verified lesson with one scheduled next bounded action, using verified event requirements src-89f188836c2c from https://openai.devpost.com/ and src-a90051657ad2 from https://openai.devpost.com/rules; data_access_status=verified.
ideas.painful_workflow: The failure is not lesson generation itself; it is that learners finish a verified checkpoint but the next action is vague, too large, or not tied to a runnable command, so progress stalls between sessions.
ideas.current_workaround: Instructors write follow-up homework in Slack, LMS comments, or a calendar invite, but the task is not automatically scoped to the learner's last passing repo state or checked against the same execution evidence.
ideas.imported_mechanism: mechanism-001: model-mediated differential testing, repurposed from finding edge cases to bounding the next learner action. GPT-5.6 performs the material planning role: it reasons over the last passing checkpoint, failed variants, and official Build Week requirement evidence to propose one small next action with acceptance criteria. Codex performs the material implementation role: it builds the scheduler, repo-state detector, command verifier, calendar/task export, and traceable session artifacts.
ideas.core_computation: The system reads a verified lesson checkpoint transcript, learner repo state, failed tests, and timebox constraints. It uses GPT-5.6 to synthesize three candidate next actions, rejects any action without a runnable acceptance command, and Codex-built verification schedules the smallest passing action into an LMS task, calendar event, or GitHub issue. Day 1: create a sample lesson repo and define a 30-minute bounded-action metric. Day 2: build checkpoint transcript parser and action schema. Day 3: add GPT-5.6 candidate generation plus invariant-based action rejection. Day 4: implement Codex-built scheduling exports to GitHub issue and calendar ICS with acceptance commands. Day 5: record a before/after demo showing vague homework converted into one scheduled, verified next step.
ideas.last_mile_action: Schedules the next bounded action instead of writing another lesson page: it creates a dated GitHub issue or ICS task with one command to run, one file region to edit, one acceptance test, and links to verified evidence IDs src-89f188836c2c and src-a90051657ad2.
ideas.visible_transformation: Before: a learner exits with 0 scheduled next actions and a vague note like 'finish the parser'. After: the system schedules 1 bounded 30-minute action, attaches 1 acceptance command, and verifies that the target repo state changes from 2/3 passing checks to 3/3 after the task is completed.
ideas.sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
ideas.technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
ideas.why_now: The submission window closes on July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT, changes are barred after that point, and Stage One can reject projects that fail basic viability or required-tool fit.
ideas.killer_demo: Start from a lesson checkpoint where the learner has a failing parser edge case and no homework item. GPT-5.6 proposes a bounded repair task, Codex writes the issue plus ICS event, the learner applies the suggested patch, and the demo counter changes from 0 scheduled verified actions and 2/3 checks passing to 1 scheduled verified action and 3/3 checks passing.
ideas.hard_to_fake_advantage: The scheduler is anchored to runnable repo evidence and a single measurable next action, so it cannot hide behind inspirational tutoring prose. The artifact exists in the learner's actual workflow as a scheduled issue or calendar task with a pass/fail command.
